- When sentiment is high (≥0.8), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reverting trend.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; apply a 1–2 day lag correction after price peaks.
- After a sharp upward move, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is rising and price is falling, model underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% to reflect sentiment momentum.
- Model fails to capture late-period mean reversion; add 1–2% downward bias in final 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
